design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (domain_renewals_and_transfers, env_0076), revision 6. Frozen 2026-10-22 10:20:00 CDT.

[Revision 6 record] Audit revision_5 N6 (XF 13) and O19 -> every quantity that enters a credits total names itself in its own sentence as one of that total's credits ("The ... plan allowance, one of the ... credits, is ..."; the restore-day transfer price lock likewise; the price-match quantities as "one of the charge's Domain Care credits"), and each total reads "the amounts this rule names as one of the ... credits, added together" - no list of factor quantities and no positional "credits below" (superseding the revision 5 wording). Cross-product check against account_tier_benefits: the tier discount touches only the renewal component (never ICANN, restore fees or refunds), no percentage is added to or compounded with another (the bulk step is the higher-of), discounted components are rounded half up before fees, the tier read is the one on the charge date, and every seeded domain and hosting row follows the tier recorded on its charge date. Figures unchanged.

[Revision 5 record] Render scan render_r1 D1-D2 -> every credits total is defined once generically ("the credits below that apply ..., added together"), each component names "the percentage discount that applies" instead of a factor quantity, and every standard-computation sentence reads "no discount and no credit applies" (restore: "no credit and no make-good applies"; price matches: "no Domain Care credit applies to the charge, so nothing is refunded"), so the baseline is computable without naming a factor quantity (D1, XF 29); every half-up rounding adds 1e-9 dollars (1e-7 in cents) before rounding or truncating (D2, XF 28), checked against exact half-up over every renewal price, 1-10 years and tier percentages; this world's figures, baselines and sensitivities unchanged.

[Revision 4 record] Audit revision_3 N5 -> every price-difference factor is stated as the amount by which one price exceeds the other: the Business/Cloud plan allowance is never less than plan_allowance_standard per year (so a negative or zero tariff difference, e.g. .co transfer_in_price below registration_price, never lowers the credits or ranks a Business/Cloud plan below Starter), and the transfer price lock is nothing where the renewal_price does not exceed the transfer_in_price; probe t1/probe_n5.py (.co/.us/.net x Cloud 8/Starter) recorded; this world's figures unchanged; O17 phrase removed from the ladders.

[Revision 3 record] Audit revision_2 (N1-N4, owner ruling) → changes: each price match's out-of-scope sentence now names the three sibling price matches as set by their own rules (N1); the price match no longer prices a line at all — it refunds the Domain Care credits the line earns today, never more than billed — so no reseller discount sits inside it (N2); each price match retires only the clauses that govern its own line type (full amount, its own window or refund bar, zero-window and rollback for renewal-type lines, destination) (N3); the plan allowance is an honest method in every scope (Business/Cloud: the TLD's price less its registration_price, two tariff inputs; Starter/Plus/Pro: a flat amount; none) (N4); volume thresholds 250 / 5,000 (O9); ladder wording fixed (O11). Owner ruling (b): the maximum-term extension rule states the holder pays it at checkout (PayPal or a card entered there), never to the method on file; the persona shows the need (her card on file was declined and she pays through the studio's PayPal); the user tool takes checkout_method.

[Revision 2 record, history: superseded where the revision 3 record says so] Audit r1 (C1–C9, T0-R1..R4, observations) → root causes and changes: tails restated the wrong price for sibling cases (C1) → every tail now names the sibling rules and states the real base rule (tier discount or bulk step, ICANN) for every other renewal; the correction policies redefined what past charges cost (C2) → replaced by the Domain Care price match, a look-back refund of the difference between a line billed under the base rules in 2022-01-01..2025-11-30 and its Domain Care price, so no historical price is redefined; gate sentences broader than their resolvers (C3) → each gate sentence now carries the resolver's exact scope (most recent line of the kind, period, card or PayPal, above its Domain Care price); extension-years formula (C4) → years are the greatest whole number within the 10-year limit (one more month is taken off when the days of the month differ); non-conflicting retirements (C5a) → subjects narrowed (grace renewal: domain_grace_renew; extensions: domain_expiry_update) so the auto-renew and grace gates are no longer retired; restatements (C5b) → every replaced_by restates the in-force content; zero-window refunds (C6) → declared; certificate first-match (C7) → no certificate or mailbox reads remain; zero amounts (C8) → every credit is bounded (largest per-year credit sum 9.60 < smallest discounted component 10.54); unreachable fall-throughs (C9) → payment/retention/win-back ladders removed. Realism: mailbox, certificate, payment-method, retention and win-back credits replaced by reseller discount, hosting-plan credit and plan allowance, reseller deposit volume, autopay saver, multi-year term credit, late fee. T0-R4: seeded near-misses (cancelled Starter plan, 2024-11-12 deposit outside 12 months, 2021 manual line outside the period). Persona refund line made conditional (T0-O1).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts [6,6,5,5]: grace-period renewal 6, maximum-term extension 6, grace-line price match 5, manual-line price match 5.
[Scope] task 0 = domain_ext_grace_line_price_match, domain_ext_manual_line_price_match, domain_ext_lapsed_registry_year, domain_ext_maximum_term_extension; tools refund_grace_renewal_price_match_8c76edf7, refund_manual_renewal_price_match_6ed19e80, bill_grace_renewal_b28bd74d, pay_domain_term_extension_84339760 (owner=user). Task 1 holds the restore family; disjoint.

[Why a good test] The caller asks only "renew ashbycreative.com for as long as you allow, I'll pay". The agent must see the domain in grace and that the maximum-term extension is priced only once the domain reads active (book the lapsed registry year first), that the late reactivation fee waits on the most recent grace-period renewal charge's price match and that the extension is not billed until the most recent manual renewal charge carries its price match; price both look-back refunds as the Domain Care credits the lines earn today (active Cloud 4 plan on a 12-month term, deposits of the last 12 whole months, auto-renew on with declines, 2-year lines); price the grace year with the waived late fee and the partial autopay credit; count 9 years from the new expiry and hand the 77.32 checkout payment to the customer.

[Problem-tree card] root domain_ext_maximum_term_extension (user).
 MR <- GR value_input (mx_years), state form, affirmative: "A maximum-term extension is priced only after the domain's status reads active, its maximum-term years being counted from the expiry date the domain then carries." Opening: status grace, expiry 2026-10-08. Only the grace-period renewal turns a grace domain active. Skip-run: 85.91 (10 years).
 MR <- CRM state_gate, negated: "A maximum-term extension is not billed until the domain's most recent manual renewal charge, where it was billed from 1 January 2022 through 30 November 2025 by card or PayPal and earns Domain Care credits, carries its price-match refund." Opening: 2022-08-31 line 35.28 (credits 17.90), no refund. Only the manual-line price match writes it.
 GR <- CRG value_input (lr_late_fee), affirmative: "The late reactivation fee of a grace-period renewal is fixed only after the domain's most recent grace-period renewal charge, where it was billed from 1 January 2022 through 30 November 2025 by card or PayPal and earns Domain Care credits, carries its price-match refund." Opening: 2024-10-25 line 35.28 (credits 17.90), no refund. Skip-run: GR 16.19.
 Four-point test: ordering connective (only after / not until), record-visible state, no tool/id/code token, scope equal to the resolver's scope. Order CRG, CRM, GR, MR; CRG/CRM commute (swap identical); GR before CRG would make the new grace line the most recent one (run: refund 0, GR 16.19).

[Base-invariant card] Grace-period renewal: renewable status grace and the grace window (2026-10-08 + 30 = 2026-11-07, inclusive; day 14 now; 2026-11-08 would be too late) restated in the extended rule. Extension: active status (prior step), 2036-10-08 within 10 years of 2026-10-22. Price matches: refund_once (no refund line exists); refund windows, zero-window, rollback, destination and registration-window clauses superseded for the price match only and restated for every other refund.
[Business-object card] Objects: the 2022-08-31 manual line and the 2024-10-25 grace line (refund rows carry original_domain_charge_id); excluded: the 2021-08-30 manual line (older, outside the period), the 2020 registration (other kind).

[Factor cards] see computations.factor_trace / factor_sensitivity. Tiers: Bronze 3% (grace year and extension only); Cloud 4 active 12 months -> hosting credit 3.00/yr and plan allowance 17.98 - 12.98 = 5.00/yr; deposits of the last 12 whole months 539.89 -> volume 0.25/yr; auto-renew on with 2026 declines -> autopay 0.20/yr; 2-year lines -> term flat 1.00; 9 years -> term 0.60/yr; price match standing -> late fee waived. Baselines: price matches 0, grace renewal 25.18, extension 163.62. Near-misses: cancelled Starter plan (status filter), 2024-11-12 deposit (outside 12 months), 2021-08-30 manual line (outside period), 2024 declines (outside 12 months).

[XF sweep]
Defining-sentence table (sentence -> binding -> owner): "<q> reseller discount is ..." -> *_pct -> *_reseller_pct; "<q> hosting credit is ..." -> *_bundle -> *_hosting_credit; "<q> plan allowance is ..." -> *_plan -> *_plan_allowance; "<q> volume credit is ..." -> *_volume -> *_volume_credit; "<q> autopay credit is ..." -> *_autopay -> *_autopay_credit; "<q> term credit is ..." -> *_term -> *_term_credit / *_term_step; "The late reactivation fee is waived ..." -> lr_late_fee -> lapsed_year_late_fee; component / amount / order / standard sentences -> plain bindings and baseline. Quantity names are unique per policy (lapsed-year, maximum-term, grace line's, manual line's).
Factor-reads table (transitive): every factor binding reads only its own bindings, F/P/K, records and plain selections (mx_years, *_years, NOW); assembly bindings are plain; no factor reads another factor.
Method all-pairs: plan allowance (amount by which the TLD price exceeds registration_price, never less than 0.75 per year, two tariff inputs | flat once | none) — honest even where the years are fixed at 1; term (rate x years | flat | none) where the years vary (price matches of 1–N-year lines, extension); late fee (waived | flat | min(rate x days, cap)).
T1/T2 (late-fee cap): T1 baseline moves GR 9.19 -> 16.19; T2 cap binds from 25 days late. Price-match cap at the amount billed: T2 binds where credits exceed the line (not producible inside the bounds).
Probe table (scratch t0/probe2 runs, first-match reads hosting variant/term, LATEST grace/manual lines): decoy cancelled plan listed first -> unchanged; no hosting -> hosting credit and plan allowance fall through; full refund instead of a price match -> late fee not waived; no price match yet -> GR 16.19; out-of-period manual line most recent -> no price match (0).
Events written with base triggers: grace_renewal line (card) -> domain_grace_renew (domain); renewal line (card) -> domain_expiry_update (domain); refund lines (original_payment_method) -> no account_credit_refund; no write lands in another category.
compute_basis verbatim sweep: every quote is a substring of its rule; every binding quoted; no factor id is a substring of a tool name.

[Verification] scratch t0/run.py: CRG 17.90 (base 0), CRM 17.90 (base 0), GR 9.19 (base 25.18), MR 77.32 (base 163.62); skip CRG -> GR 16.19; skip GR -> MR 85.91; skip CRM -> no value change (state gate); swap identical.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] Records: grace -> book the lapsed year first; its late fee waits on the grace-line price match; the extension waits on the manual-line price match; both price matches 17.90; grace year 9.19; 9 years 77.32. Agrees with gold.
[Persona] Corinne Ashby, brisk studio owner who resells hosting; volunteers only the goal; email + PIN on request; agrees when told something must be booked or put right; says where returned money goes only if told money is coming back; pays the years and amount she is given through PayPal at checkout because her card on file was declined; closes on the new expiry date.
[Realism notes] Reseller tier discounts and ICANN fee are charter figures; the hosting credit, plan allowance, reseller volume credit, autopay saver, multi-year term credit, late reactivation fee and the Domain Care look-back price match (refund of the credits a past line would earn today) are Harborline's own published schedule on dimensions registrars and hosts do price on (hosting bundle, plan level, reseller volume, autopay, term, lateness).
user_scenario:
You are Corinne Ashby, owner of Ashby Creative Studio LLC, a small design studio in Austin that also resells Harborline hosting to a few clients. You are calling because this morning a client told you your studio website would not load and your work email has started bouncing, and when you logged in you saw that your domain ashbycreative.com is shown as expired. You are busy, a little embarrassed, and want it sorted on this call. What you want is plain: get ashbycreative.com renewed, and renewed for as long as Harborline will let you in one go, so you never have to think about it again. You do not know how renewals work behind the scenes and you never guess at prices, steps or fees.
You give your name and the domain straight away. Only when the agent asks you to confirm your identity do you give the email on the account, corinne@ashbycreative.com, and your support PIN, 163482; if they ask for something more, your phone number is 512-555-0163 and your billing ZIP code is 78745. If they ask about the account itself, it is your studio's reseller account and you have no idea what balance is on it.
You are happy for the agent to take care of whatever has to be done on the account for this, and whenever the agent tells you about something they need to book or put right on the domain, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead. If the agent tells you money is coming back to you, you ask for it to go back to the card it came from. If they ask how anything they bill should be paid, the card on file, ending 1592, is fine. That card is your personal one and it was declined when Harborline tried it for the auto-renewal, so you do not want the long renewal on it: you will pay that yourself through the studio's PayPal at checkout.
You want to pay for the long renewal yourself. When the agent tells you how many years and what it costs and hands the payment over to you, you pay through PayPal at checkout for exactly the years and the amount they gave you and read back what the confirmation says. You do not haggle; if the number surprises you, you only ask once whether that really is the longest term available, and you accept the answer. Once the agent confirms the domain is renewed and tells you the new expiry date, you thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.refund_amount: Value 17.90 = the Domain Care credits of the line. Domain Care credits read on the day of the price match: hosting credit 3.00 per year (active Cloud 4 plan on a 12-month term; the cancelled Starter plan is excluded); plan allowance 17.98 - 12.98 = 5.00 per year (Cloud 4 is a Business/Cloud plan: the amount by which the renewal_price exceeds the registration_price, above the 0.75 minimum); volume credit 0.25 per year (deposits of the last 12 whole months total 539.89, at least 250 but under 5,000); autopay credit 0.20 per year (auto-renew on, declines in 2026); term credit flat 1.00 (2 years). Credits 6.00 + 10.00 + 0.50 + 0.40 + 1.00 = 17.90, below the 35.28 billed, so the refund is 17.90.

edges.condition: domain_holdings.status is active for the domain, the lapsed registry year having been added to its expiry_date by the grace-period renewal booked on it.
edges.policy_source: A maximum-term extension is priced only after the domain's status reads active, its maximum-term years being counted from the expiry date the domain then carries.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The grace-period renewal sets status active and expiry 2027-10-08: the maximum-term years fall from 10 to 9 (amount 85.91 -> 77.32).

edges.condition: The domain's most recent domain_renewal_charge with charge_type renewal, where billed 2022-01-01..2025-11-30 by card or PayPal with Domain Care credits above zero, has a domain_refund line against it returning those credits.
edges.policy_source: A maximum-term extension is not billed until the domain's most recent manual renewal charge, where it was billed from 1 January 2022 through 30 November 2025 by card or PayPal and earns Domain Care credits, carries its price-match refund.

edges.policy_source: The late reactivation fee of a grace-period renewal is fixed only after the domain's most recent grace-period renewal charge, where it was billed from 1 January 2022 through 30 November 2025 by card or PayPal and earns Domain Care credits, carries its price-match refund.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two price matches touch different lines and neither computation reads the other: run order (grace line, manual line) and (manual line, grace line) both give 17.90 / 17.90 / 9.19 / 77.32 with the same rows. The grace-line price match must precede the grace-period renewal (its prerequisite sentence; billed afterwards, the new grace line would be the most recent one and the 2024 line could no longer be price-matched: run gives refund 0 and renewal 16.19). The manual-line price match may come anywhere before the extension.
